---
title: "OSMnx · Elevation, DEM & 3D terrain (La Paz)"
---

::: {.lead}
A 3D urban terrain for **Avenida Naciones Unidas, La Paz** within a 2 km radius.
La Paz is the reference case because its relief makes the DEM pipeline, node
elevations and street grades obvious at a glance. Mirrors the
[Elevation panel](../../../panels/osmnx/elevation.qmd).
:::

Needs internet access unless you supply a local GeoTIFF. An OpenTopography API
key gives the best DEM quality; Open-Elevation works without one.

## 1. Download the area (2 km radius)

In **Download**, use **Point** (or **Address**) with the location near Avenida
Naciones Unidas and **Distance** `2000` m, then **Project Graph** in
[Graph Operations](graph-operations.qmd).

![Downloading a 2 km radius around Avenida Naciones Unidas, La Paz.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/09-download-lapaz.png)

## 2. Get elevation data

Under **1 · Get Elevation Data**, pick a **DEM Source** (**OpenTopography**,
**Open-Elevation**, or **Local GeoTIFF** with a **Local Path**), enable **Apply
to Nodes** and **Create Terrain**, and set **Vertical Scale**. API sources also
take an **API Resolution** and a **Workers** count.

![The Get Elevation controls with a DEM source selected.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/09-get-elevation.png)

::: {.callout-note}
**Export AOI** writes the area of interest out, which is what you need to fetch a
Copernicus DEM tile for the local GeoTIFF route.
:::

## 3. Apply 3D positions

Conforms the network to the terrain surface, draping the streets across the
slopes.

![The network draped onto La Paz terrain.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/09-apply-3d.png)

## 4. Add edge grades

Computes each edge's slope (`grade`) and its absolute value (`grade_abs`). La
Paz's steep streets produce high grades.

![Edge grades colored along the streets.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/09-grades.png)

## 5. Elevation-aware routing

In [Routing](routing.qmd), set **Path Weight** to **elevation_impedance** and
choose an **Alpha**. The cost becomes `length * (1 + alpha * |grade|)`, so steep
climbs are penalized and flatter detours win. Compare against a plain **length**
route to see how far the detour goes.

![Comparing a flat-preferring route against a length-only route.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/09-elevation-routing.png)

## 6. Add a basemap

Under **5 · Basemap Texture**, choose a **Source** and a **Zoom**, then
**Fetch & Apply**.

![Satellite imagery draped over the La Paz terrain.](../../../assets/guides/osmnx/09-basemap.png)

## Next steps

[Basemaps & API textures](basemaps.qmd) reuses this terrain to compare imagery
sources, WMS layers and zoom levels.
